transcript.text: Hello, I'm Ryota, and welcome to your English lesson! Today we'll talk about your work and a recent project, practise the present perfect and the past simple, and finish with some conversation. Does that sound good to you?
Yeah, sure.

Great, let's begin. Today you'll talk about your job and a project you're proud of, and we'll practise two grammar points: the "present perfect" for experience that continues now, and the "past simple" for things that finished at a specific time. I'll correct your mistakes, explain them, and give you a chance to try again. At the end you can practise your pronunciation if you like. First comes a short, one-time level check, so I can adjust the lesson for you. Are you ready?
Uh, yes.
First, a short, friendly chat so I can see what you can already do. Please answer in English, and don't worry about mistakes.
Uh, I sales manager, Nagoya Corporation, sell washing machine.
Thank you. You sell washing machines for Nagoya Corporation. Now, next question: have you ever worked with a customer from another country? If so, tell me a little about it. If not, that's fine too.
Yes, I work with uh Canada customer, sell 25 washing machine.
That's a good result, 25 washing machines for a Canadian customer! Next question: what is one skill you'd like to improve in your English, and why is it important to you?
I want uh talk to international customer fluent English uh improve communication.
Talking with international customers more smoothly is a very useful goal. Today we'll make your sentences clearer and more natural. ここまでで、レベル確認は終わりです。次は「Your job」、仕事について話す練習です。質問がありますか、それとも次に進みましょうか。
Yes.

仕事について話すときは、短い文を使いましょう。「I work in…」は「私は…で働いています」という意味です。

例えば「I work in sales.」は「私は営業で働いています」です。では、あなたの仕事について、一文か二文で言ってみてください。最初は「I work…」から始めてみましょう。

 What do you do at work?
I work at home appliance division at Nagoya Corporation.
「the」が抜けています。「I work in the home appliance division」と言います。 もう一度言ってみてください。
I work in the home appliance division at Nagoya Corporation.

そうです、正しく言えました。「I work in the home appliance division at Nagoya Corporation.」です。

Next, let's talk about what you sell. Please say one sentence, starting with "I sell".

What do you sell at Nagoya Corporation?
I I sell washing machine at Nagoya Corporation.
「washing machine」は、数が複数のときは「machines」と最後に s を付けます。 もう一度言ってみてください。
I sell washing machines at Nagoya Corporation.
そうです、正しく言えました。 I sell washing machines at Nagoya Corporation. 仕事について話す練習は、ここまでです。次は「Present perfect」、現在完了です。質問がありますか。それとも、次に進みましょうか。
Yes.

現在完了は、過去に始まって今も続いている経験や期間を話すときに使います。形は「have / has + 過去分詞」です。

それでは、質問です。

Have you worked for your current company for a long time?
Uh, yes, I work here at Nagoya Corporation 6 years.

「I work here」だと今の状態だけになります。六年前から今も働いているので、現在完了を使います。「I have worked here at Nagoya Corporation for six years.」と言いましょう。

では、この文をもう一度言ってみてください。
I have worked here at Nagoya Corporation for 6 years.

そうです、正しく言えました。 I have worked here at Nagoya Corporation for six years. 六年前から今も続いているので、現在完了です。

では、別の言い方で聞きます。あなたの仕事は何ですか。

What is your job at Nagoya Corporation?
Uh, my job is uh sales manager uh and sell washing machines.

「and I sell」と、「I」を入れます。

次は現在完了で質問します。「あなたは営業マネージャーになってどのくらいですか」という質問です。答えは「I have been a sales manager for…」で始めてみてください。
I have been a sales manager for 6 year.

「have been」と現在完了を正しく使えました。ただ、「6 year」は「6 years」と複数にします。

もう一度、言ってみてください。
I have been a sales manager for 6 years.

そうです、正しく言えました。"I have been a sales manager for six years." は、今も続いている経験の文です。

現在完了の練習はここまでです。次は「Past simple」、過去形です。質問がありますか。
Yes.

過去形は、終わった出来事を、「yesterday」や「last year」のような時を表す言葉と一緒に話すときに使います。では質問です。

Did you attend any business events or exhibitions last year?
Yes. I attend robotics exhibition in Tokyo. last year.
「last year」があるので過去形を使います。「attend」は「attended」になります。 もう一度言ってみてください。
I attended a robotics exhibition in Tokyo last year.

Yes, that's right. You used the past simple with "last year."

質問です。去年、どんな製品を売りましたか。答えは「I sold…」で始めてみてください。

 What products did you sell last year?
I sell uh washing machine and hair dryer last year.
「sell」の過去形は「sold」です。 もう一度、言ってみてください。
Ah, I sold washing machines and hair dryers last year.

Yes, that's right. You used the past simple with "last year" correctly. 去年の話なので、過去形ですね。

 When did you first meet your Canadian customer?

Start with: "I first met…"
I first met uh Canadian customer um 6 month ago.
at airport.

すばらしいです！ "I first met" と過去形を正しく使えています。 「6 month」は「6 months」と、複数の s を付けます。

では、次の質問です。そのお客様と何について話しましたか。「We discussed…」で始めてみてください。

 What did you discuss with the customer?
Start with: "We discussed…"
We discussed how to sell washing machines to Canada customers.

「We discussed」は過去形で正しく言えています。「カナダのお客様」は「Canadian customers」と言います。

これで過去形の練習は終わりです。次は「Conversation」、会話の練習です。質問がありますか。
Canadian customers.

そうです、"Canadian customers" と言えています。これで過去形の練習は終わりです。次は「Conversation」、会話の練習です。

Ready to go on, or would you like to ask something first?
Uh, yes.

では、会話の練習をしましょう。質問に、英語で答えてください。

How long have you been at Nagoya Corporation?
Um, I work Nagoya Corporation uh 7 year.

「I work」だと今の仕事だけになります。七年前から今も続いているので、「have worked」を使います。

もう一度、言ってみてください。
I have worked at Nagoya Corporation

そうです、正しく言えました。期間を入れると、さらに分かりやすくなります。

仕事で一番好きなことは何ですか。

 What do you like most about your job?
Uh, the most about my job is um talking international customer world over.

世界中のお客様と話せるのは、いいですね。どうしてそれが一番好きなのですか。

 Why do you like talking with international customers?
Uh, give me um international exposure and growth.

International experience helps you grow, and that's a good reason to enjoy your work. We say "It gives me…" when the subject is a thing or idea.

 It gives me international exposure and growth.

Can you tell me about one thing you learned from an international customer?
I learn how to drive car. Canadian customer, teach me.

Wow, a Canadian customer taught you to drive! That's a story I'd like to hear more about.

What was it like learning to drive with your customer?
Uh, it was good. Uh, I showed him Tokyo and he liked very much.

That sounds like a great day out. Tokyo is a big city, so I can imagine how much he enjoyed it.

What did he enjoy most in Tokyo, and how did you show him around?
Uh, he liked the Tokyo zoo and the uh animals and Panda.

Pandas are a favourite for many visitors, and I like zoos too. On weekends I often go hiking near Gifu, and I see animals there as well.

Now it's your turn to ask me a question about work or your experience. What would you like to know?
Uh, I want to know about your family and what you do.

I'm happy to tell you about my work. I have taught English in Nagoya for about eight years, and I help Japanese professionals speak English. I'd like to keep my family private, though. 家族の話は控えさせてください。

Why did you choose to work in sales?
I like meeting new people and helping them.

That's a lovely reason, and it's clear. "I like meeting new people and helping them" is a complete, natural sentence.

Can you tell me about a time when you helped a new customer? What happened?
Uh, yes. Um, one Mr. Kenji wanted top load machine. I tell him front load better saves electricity. He buy it.

Mr. Kenji wanted a top-load machine, and you told him about the electricity savings. He bought it.

Did he use the machine at home? What did he say about it?
Yes, he use machine at home. Uh, he came back to thank me for it.

That's a kind thing for him to do, and it's a good story about your work.

What did he say to you when he came back?
He tell me that he has uh good experience with machine. His wife likes it.

Good to hear it worked so well for him, and that his wife likes it too.

What does his wife like about the machine, and why?
Um, his wife say the clothes dry fast and clothes are cleaner.

Quick drying and cleaner clothes are two good reasons to buy a machine. Conversation practice is done. Next is Pronunciation, which is optional. Would you like to practise it, or go straight to the summary? Or do you have a question first?
Yes.
Okay, conversation is done. Next is pronunciation. Shall we go on, or do you have a question first?
Yes.

発音の練習を始めましょう。次の四つから選んでください。

どれにしますか。番号か、言葉で答えてください。

You can choose: 1) individual words, 2) a complete sentence, 3) speaking more naturally, or 4) skip and continue.
Complete sentence.

いいですね、一文の練習にしましょう。まず私が言うので、あとに続けて言ってください。

I have worked with international customers for several years.
I have worked with international customers for several years.
もう一度、ゆっくり言ってみてください。
I have worked with international customers for several years.

Your second try scored 84 out of 100. The weakest sounds were "with" and "for", so keep those short and clear. Here is the whole sentence from me once more: I have worked with international customers for several years.

Great work today! You talked about your job, your responsibilities and your experience. One thing you did well was "I have worked at Nagoya Corporation for seven years", which uses the present perfect correctly. One thing to improve is the number of years: you said "6 year", and we say "six years".

 I have worked here for six years.

Before we finish, can you explain the difference between these two sentences? I have worked here for five years. I worked here five years ago. Take your time, and I'll help if you need it.
I have worked here for 5 years, means I still work here and the other one means I don't work here anymore.

そうです、その通りです。一つ目は今も働いている意味で、二つ目は五年前に働いていて、今は終わったという意味です。ひとつだけ、「5 years」は「five years」と書きます。

ここまでで、何か質問はありますか。
Uh, no question.

Thank you, Praveen. You talked about your job and a project you're proud of, and you used the present perfect and past simple well. Keep practising "I have worked here for…" when you talk about your experience. Goodbye, and see you next time!
